sentences.text: Shri Navneet Kishore Verma, learned counsel for the   Santosh Purohit, learned counsel for the respondent
Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent   Shri Nikhil Baghela, learned counsel for the respond  ORDER

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act passed in Claim Case No.24/2015 challenging the quantum of compensation as well as total exoneration of the Insurance Company.

2. Short facts of the case are that on 16.5.2013 at around 12.20 deceased Deepak was coming through his motorcycle, when he reached near Bhouransa Phata, the vehicle Toofan No.MP-42-BC-0361 came from the side of Dewas, which was coming from wrong side, the respondent No.1 was driving the same in rash and negligent manner.
He dashed into the motorcycle of Deepak, because of which he sustained grievous injuries due to which he succumbed to injuries and died on 5.8.2013.

2.1. The appellants-claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21606 2 MA-1452-2016 Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Deepak, who was their son.

entities.text:
NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21606 2 MA-1452-2016 Motor Vehicles Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The claims Tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.12,14,555/-, but exonerated the Insurance Company from liability from paying compensation on the ground that the offending vehicle was private vehicle and used for commercial use.

3. The submission of the counsel for the appellant is that while assessing income of the deceased no amount for future prospects has been added, although at the time of accident deceased was 26 years of age.

It is also submitted that claims Tribunal has concluded that the offending vehicle was operated as a taxi, whereas it was registered as a private vehicle and the insurance policy was also Smt. sentences.text: He submits that Tribunal should have directed to pay and recover.

Ashwini Sinha and others) and order dated 29.1.2025 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.1175/2025 (M.Ananthi and others Vs. P.Venkaresan and another).
4.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company supports the findings of the award.

He submits that it was duly proved that the offending vehicle was operated as a taxi, whereas it was registered as private vehicle and the insurance police was also issued NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21606 3 MA-1452-2016 for a private vehicle, thus there is no liability of the Insurance Company.
Thus, the direction to pay and recover could not have been issued.
4.1. In support of his contention he relies on the judgment of this Court in the case of Oriental Fire and General Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pramila and others, reported in AIR 1989 MP 49 .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

It is seen from the record that the claims Tribunal while calculating income of the deceased in para 27 of the award has not made any addition for future prospects, whereas the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ SC 2700, has held that addition in the income has to be made for future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ SC 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, looking to the age of deceased between 26 to 30 years in terms of findings of para 24 of the award, 40% is to be added in the income of the deceased.
The claims Tribunal has calculated compensation for loss of dependency at Rs.5,44,000/-.

The 40% of the same would come to Rs.2,17,000/-.
7.
As regards liability of the Insurance Company from the record it is clear that the offending vehicle was registered as private vehicle, which is evident from Ex.D/1, which is the insurance policy.

However, in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Pushkar Mehra,
M.Ananthi (supra) and considering the fact that the claimants cannot be made to run from pillar to post for collecting compensation when the Insurance Company has insured the vehicle and it is the fault of the owner that it was run in breach of the conditions of the policy.

It is directed that the Insurance Company shall first pay the amount of compensation to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21606 4 MA-1452-2016 appellants-claimants and then can recover the same from owner of the vehicle.

Even in the case relied by counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company in para 32 it was mentioned by this Court that the Insurance Company shall not be entitled to restitution of compensation from claimants, but it can recover from the owner and the driver.
Thus, in that case pay and recover was very much present.
8. In view of the above analysis the appellants are entitled for payment of further amount of Rs.2,17,000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.

sentences.text: The Insurance Company is directed to first pay the entire amount of compensation and then it may recover the same from the owner and driver of the vehicle.
9. With the aforesaid direction, the present Misc.Appeal stands disposed off.
